## 👋 Welcome!

My name is **Jiahao Tian**. I am an undergraduate student majoring in Statistics at the [School of Mathematical Sciences](http://www.math.zju.edu.cn), **Zhejiang University**.

My academic interests lie at the intersection of high-dimensional inference, uncertainty quantification, and theoretical statistics. I am particularly interested in developing statistically principled methods that remain reliable under heavy-tailed distributions, covariate shift, and other forms of model misspecification.

My coursework includes advanced probability, mathematical statistics, real and functional analysis, stochastic processes, stochastic differential equations, and asymptotic statistics.

## 🛰️ [Research Experience](Projects/index.qmd)

### **Heavy-Tailed Robustness of Multiple-Knockoff Aggregation Methods**
* **Advisor:** [Prof. Lijun Wang](https://hohoweiya.xyz/), Zhejiang University. *(Sep. 2025 – Present)*

* Conducted a systematic robustness study of e-value-, voting-, p-value-, and data-splitting-based knockoff aggregation methods under Gaussian, moderately heavy-tailed, and Cauchy regimes.
* Identified a **zero-dilution mechanism** in which unstable and severely truncated single-run selections cause occasional signal discoveries to be diluted below the final aggregation threshold.
* Developed an asymptotic explanation using regular variation, exact null sign symmetry, concentration inequalities, and Extreme Value Theory, linking multiplicity-driven threshold inflation to vanishing signal-selection probabilities in sparse high-dimensional regimes.
* Investigated robust feature statistics and efficient calibration of the internal knockoff threshold.

* *Status: First-author manuscript in preparation.*

### **Distributional Balancing Weights for Conformal Calibration under Covariate Shift**
* **Advisor:** [Prof. Guanhua Chen](https://sites.google.com/view/gchenwisc/), UW–Madison. *(Mar. 2026 – Present)*

* Developed a distributionally balanced conformal calibration framework that uses response-free weights to align source calibration covariates with an unlabeled target sample.
* Specialized the framework to **Characteristic Function Distance (CFD)** balancing and used Fourier analysis to study how spectral decay affects the representation of covariate-dependent conformity-score distributions.
* Implemented the method for **Split Conformal Prediction**, **CQR**, **UACQR-S**, and **UACQR-P**.
* Contributed to the technical verification and revision of a general score-distribution and approximate coverage-error bound involving residual imbalance, function-class approximation, finite target-sample uncertainty, and effective sample size.
* Designed theory-aligned simulations examining coverage, interval efficiency, score-distribution error, imbalance, and weight concentration under varying overlap and score smoothness.

* *Status: First-author manuscript in preparation.*
